page: Microsoft Azure F48ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine engineered for compute-heavy workloads requiring dedicated execution threads and fast temporary I/O. Driven by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates 48 physical x86_64 cores without multithreading from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Each core includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and access to 32 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions. System memory provides 192 GB of total capacity, maintaining a 4 GB per core allocation.

Storage architecture includes a bundled 5669 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, eliminating external disk latency for high-speed scratch processing and caching tiers. The instance delivers high benchmark results, ranking in the top 10% across stress-ng single-core (3790.09) and multi-core (176118.25) suites, as well as PassMark CPU operations (99383.69). Memory read bandwidth reaches 9372.72 GB/s on small cached blocks and maintains 317.32 GB/s uncached throughput, yielding top-tier performance for memory-intensive operations such as Redis SET handling at 135.87 million operations per second.

In compiled workloads and data processing, the instance achieved 74261 in Clang software compilation and top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 687.11 GB/s. While capable of executing CPU-based small and medium language models, large 70B parameter inference yields 4.37 tokens per second text generation due to the absence of dedicated GPUs. The integrated 5.6 TB NVMe array provides significant cost efficiency for temporary disk-intensive architectures, making the F48ads_v7 well aligned with continuous integration builds, distributed caching clusters, relational database execution, and heavy batch compute jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure F48ads_v7 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz with dedicated physical cores and no simultaneous multithreading. Equipped with 192 GB of RAM (4 GB per core) and bundled with 5669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, the instance combines dense compute throughput with substantial temporary I/O capabilities. Its AMD Zen-based architecture features AVX-512 vector support with VNNI and BF16 extensions. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier execution across single-core and multi-core tests, PassMark CPU suites, software compilation, and in-memory key-value processing reaching 135.87 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking hardware accelerators, large-parameter model inference exhibits lower throughput, making this instance best fitted for parallel software compilation, batch compute processing, large-scale Redis caching, and fast local database scratch workloads.
